Require $p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2=P$ and $s=h(P,P)>4m^2$, with $h$ as in [[def-qft-example-data]]. Evaluate the coefficient map in a center-of-momentum frame $\Lambda P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$ as defined in [[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. For one scalar initial label of weight $1$ and one specified final channel, take the dimensionless real quartic tree amplitude $\mathcal A=-\lambda$. The coefficient map of [[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]] gives
$$\frac{d\sigma_{\mathrm{coeff}}}{d\Omega} =\frac{\lambda^2(\hbar c)^2}{128\pi^2s}, \qquad \sigma_{\mathrm{coeff}}=\frac{\lambda^2(\hbar c)^2}{32\pi s}$$
for identical final scalars integrated over the full labeled sphere. For distinguishable final scalars the two coefficients are twice these values.

**Given:** Assume the shell, phase-space, flux, symmetry-factor, and coefficient-map conventions of [[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. For scattering, take $p_1,p_2,k_1,k_2$ on the positive $m$-shell with $p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2=P$ and $h(P,P)=s>4m^2$; use one initial scalar label with weight $1$, one specified final channel, the displayed constant amplitude, and the center-of-momentum evaluation of the coefficient map from [[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the transverse space $\mathcal H_T=\operatorname{Ran}M_{P_T}$ of [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]], with $P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-\mathbf n\mathbf n^T$ for $\mathbf k\ne0$ and any assigned value at the null point $\mathbf k=0$. In the QFT length convention, assign $\mathbf k$ units m$^{-1}$ and define the nonnegative measurable multiplier
$$ \omega(\mathbf k):=|\mathbf k|. $$
Its maximal multiplication operator on $\mathcal H_T$ is
$$ (M_\omega f)(\mathbf k):=\omega(\mathbf k)f(\mathbf k),\qquad D(M_\omega):=\{f\in\mathcal H_T:\omega f\in L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3)\}. $$
Because $\omega$ is a scalar multiplier, $\mathbf k\cdot f(\mathbf k)=0$ a.e. implies $\mathbf k\cdot(M_\omega f)(\mathbf k)=0$ a.e.; thus the displayed multiplication maps its stated domain into $\mathcal H_T$. The value $\omega(0)=0$ is immaterial to the $L^2$ operator. For $\hbar,c>0$, the corresponding one-particle energy convention is $E_1:=\hbar c M_\omega$, in joules.

[F1] [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]] defines $\mathcal H_T=\operatorname{Ran}M_{P_T}$ as the vector-valued $L^2$ subspace with $\mathbf k\cdot f(\mathbf k)=0$ a.e.; the draft carrier exists and is listed in the QFT-MG01 manifest. This mathematical use retains its supplier hypotheses and does not itself confer independent acceptance.

Let $C_0=-i\Delta_0$, where $\Delta_0$ is the massless scalar causal commutator of [[lem-qft-scalar-causal-commutator]]. As distributions in $x-y$,
$$[E_i(x),E_j(y)]=[B_i(x),B_j(y)] =(-\delta_{ij}\Delta+\partial_i\partial_j)C_0(x-y),$$
$$[E_i(x),B_j(y)]=\epsilon_{jri}\partial_0\partial_rC_0(x-y).$$
Every right-hand side has support in the closed causal cone. Hence compactly supported tests whose supports are spacelike separated in the stated Minkowski sense give commuting field-strength operators on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. The quotient representation of [[lem-qft-photon-covariance-spectrum]] makes these smeared field strengths Lorentz covariant: their on-shell coefficient depends on a polarization class only through $p_a\epsilon_b-p_b\epsilon_a$. These conclusions concern gauge-invariant free observables and do not assert locality of the Coulomb potential.
[F2] The Lorentz action on the physical quotient is induced by $[\epsilon(p)]\mapsto[\Lambda\epsilon(\Lambda^{-1}p)]$. [[lem-qft-photon-covariance-spectrum]]

Assume Countable Choice and use the Minkowski coordinates and separation condition of [[lem-qft-photon-local-field-strength]], so $\eta(x-y,x-y)=|\mathbf x-\mathbf y|^2-(x^0-y^0)^2$. A spacetime region $O$ means an open subset of $\mathbb R^4$ in its standard topology. A real antisymmetric test $h=(h^{ab})$ is supported in $O$ when each component $h^{ab}\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb R)$ has support contained in $O$. Two open regions $O_1,O_2$ are spacelike separated when $\eta(x-y,x-y)>0$ for every $x\in O_1$ and $y\in O_2$. Let $g_h\in\mathcal H_T$ be the one-particle vector for such a test from [[lem-qft-photon-local-field-strength]]. The space $\mathcal H_T$ is separable: it is the range of the bounded projection $P_T$ on the separable space $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$. Define
$$W_O(h)=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2\,g_h),$$
where $W_{\rm Segal}$ is the Weyl unitary of [[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]]. It is bounded and unitary, and its one-parameter group has the self-adjoint field-strength closure as generator. For every open region $O\subseteq\mathbb R^4$, let $\mathcal A(O)$ be the norm-closed unital $*$-algebra generated by $W_O(h)$ for real antisymmetric tests supported in $O$; equivalently its bounded real and imaginary parts are included as observables. If $O_1,O_2$ are spacelike separated by the stated Minkowski condition, then $\mathcal A(O_1)$ and $\mathcal A(O_2)$ commute.
[F1] A compact real antisymmetric test defines $F(h)=a(g_h)+a^\dagger(g_h)$, and spacelike-separated field-strength tests commute. [[lem-qft-photon-local-field-strength]]

exact_direct_use_paragraphs:
Assume Countable Choice and use $\mathcal H_T$ from [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]]. On $\mathcal K=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^4)$ define
$$[\epsilon,\delta]_\eta=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\epsilon(\mathbf k)^\dagger\eta\,\delta(\mathbf k)\,d^3\mathbf k,\qquad \eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1).$$
For $\mathbf k\ne0$, let $n=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and set
$$\mathcal K_0=\{\epsilon\in\mathcal K:-\epsilon^0+n\cdot\boldsymbol\epsilon=0\text{ a.e.}\},\qquad T\epsilon=\boldsymbol\epsilon-n\epsilon^0.$$
Then $\mathcal K_0$ is closed, $T:\mathcal K_0\to\mathcal H_T$ is bounded and onto, and
$$[\epsilon,\delta]_\eta=\langle T\epsilon,T\delta\rangle_2\quad(\epsilon,\delta\in\mathcal K_0).$$
Its radical (the vectors pairing to zero with all of $\mathcal K_0$) is
$$\mathcal N=\ker T=\{b(\mathbf k)(1,n(\mathbf k)):b\in L^2(\mathbb R^3)\}.$$
Consequently $\mathcal K_0/\mathcal N$ with the induced form is a positive Hilbert space isometric to $\mathcal H_T$. The form on the four-component auxiliary space is indefinite; only the subsidiary quotient is the positive physical one-particle space.
**Given:** Countable Choice and the transverse Hilbert space and projector of [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]].
[F1] $P_T(\mathbf k)=I-nn^T$ is an orthogonal projection with closed range $n^\perp$ for almost every $\mathbf k\ne0$. [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]]

$$g_j(\mathbf k)=\frac{1}{(2\pi)^{3/2}(2\omega)^{1/2}}\, P_T(\mathbf k)\int_{\mathbb R^4}j(x)e^{i\omega x^0-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}\,d^4x.$$
Then $g_j\in\mathcal H_T$. On the finite-particle domain $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ of the bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathcal H_T)$, the smeared transverse potential is
$$A_T(j)=a(g_j)+a^\dagger(g_j).$$
Its matrix elements are continuous in the test-function topology; it is an operator-valued distribution and does not assign a pointwise operator to $A_i(x)$. With $E_i=-\partial_0A_i$, the equal-time canonical commutator is the distribution
$$[A_i(0,\mathbf x),E_j(0,\mathbf y)] =-i\,P_{T,ij}(-i\nabla_{\mathbf x})\delta^3(\mathbf x-\mathbf y).$$
[F1] $P_T$ is an orthogonal projection of norm at most one and $\mathcal H_T$ is its closed range. [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]]

exact_direct_use_paragraphs:
Let $K(z;\zeta)=K_0(\zeta)+zV(\zeta)$ and $S(z;\zeta)$ be the finite-dimensional formal matrices of [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]], with $d\ge1$, $K_0(\zeta)$ invertible, and both coefficient matrices covariant under the vertex phase angles of [[def-qft-qed-finite-graph-gauge-data]]. Then $S$ is a two-sided inverse of $K$ in $M_d(\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket)$, and
$$ S(z;\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta S(z;\zeta)D_\theta^{-1} $$
coefficientwise. For a real vertex tuple $\theta$, put
$\Theta:=\operatorname{diag}_{x\in X}(\theta_xI_r)$,
$\zeta_s:=\zeta^{s\theta}$, and $D_s:=D_{s\theta}=e^{is\Theta}$.
Write $K_s:=K(z;\zeta_s)$ and $S_s:=S(z;\zeta_s)$, and define
$\delta K:=\left.\frac{d}{ds}K_s\right|_{s=0}$ and
$\delta S:=\left.\frac{d}{ds}S_s\right|_{s=0}$ coefficientwise along this
differentiable phase path. The variations satisfy
$$ \delta K=i[\Theta,K],\qquad \delta S=i[\Theta,S]=-S(\delta K)S . $$
For ordinary finite matrices $A,B\in GL_d(\mathbb C)$, the corresponding resolvent identity is $B^{-1}(B-A)A^{-1}=A^{-1}-B^{-1}$. These are formal or finite algebraic statements; they assert no convergence of a perturbation series, continuum limit, or loop Ward identity.

[F1] [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]]: $K=K_0+zV$ and $S=\sum_{n\ge0}(-zK_0^{-1}V)^nK_0^{-1}$ are defined in the formal power-series ring $\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket$; each coefficient of $S$ is a finite matrix.

exact_direct_use_paragraphs:
Let $R=\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket$, let $d\ge1$, and let $K\in M_d(R)$ be a finite matrix as in [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]]. With $\mathcal I_d$ the top-coefficient functional of [[def-qft-qed-finite-grassmann-algebra]],
$$ \mathcal I_d\!\left(\exp\!\left(-\sum_{i,j=1}^d\bar\psi_iK_{ij}\psi_j\right)\right)=\det K. $$
If $D=\operatorname{diag}(u_1,\ldots,u_d)$ with each $u_i\in R^\times$ and $K'=DKD^{-1}$, then the finite Grassmann integral and determinant are gauge invariant: $\mathcal I_d(\exp(-\bar\psi K'\psi))=\det K'=\det K$. No infinite-dimensional Grassmann measure, continuum limit, or anomaly claim is made.
[F2] [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]] defines $\det K$ by the finite Leibniz sum and the diagonal vertex-phase conjugation convention.

distinguishable particles, integrated over the full labeled sphere. When

channel, threshold, and approximation are part of the model statement. No

For the scalar examples, separately adopt the constant formal amplitudes
$\mathcal A=-\lambda$ for the quartic contact channel and $\mathcal G=G_E$
for the cubic parent decay, with the units and external normalization stated
at each use. The scalar scattering inputs lie on their stated positive

conditions. For decay, the parent is $P_0=(\mathsf M_0,\mathbf0)$,
$\mathsf M_0>\mathsf M_1+\mathsf M_2$, and its two positive-shell daughters
sum to $P_0$. Their coefficient map is the one in
[[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. If a rate $\Gamma$ is reported as

does not supply a survival law.

Minkowski chart $x=(ct,\mathbf x)$, the geometric metric
$\eta=(-,+,+,+)$, and the distinct algebraic contraction
$h=-\eta=(+,-,-,-)$ of [[def-qft-example-data]]. Let $m,M\geq0$ be the

four-vector is
$q=(E,\mathbf q)\in\mathbb R^4$ with $E>0$; it has rest energy $\mathsf M\geq0$
when $h(q,q)=\mathsf M^2$. All four-vector components are in joules, and
$\mathbf q$ is $c$ times physical spatial momentum. Let $p_1,p_2$ be future electron
and positron energy four-vectors with rest energy $m$, and $k_1,k_2$ future
muon and antimuon energy four-vectors with rest energy $M$, satisfying
$p_1+p_2=k_1+k_2=P$ and
$$ s=h(P,P)>4\max(m^2,M^2). $$
By [[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]], choose a proper orthochronous
$h$-Lorentz matrix $\Lambda\in GL(4,\mathbb R)$, meaning
$\Lambda^Th\Lambda=h$, $\det\Lambda=1$, and preservation of the future
causal cone $C_+:=\{(E,\mathbf q):E>0,\ h((E,\mathbf q),(E,\mathbf q))\geq0\}$,
with $\Lambda P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$.
Its boost construction supplies such a map because $P$ is future timelike.
The **center-of-momentum inertial chart** has coordinates
$x^{\rm CM}=\Lambda x$ on spacetime and corresponding four-vector components
$q^{\rm CM}=\Lambda q$; from here on, four-vector components are in that
chart, so $P=(\sqrt{s},\mathbf0)$. The strict threshold makes
$\mathbf p_1$ and $\mathbf k_1$ nonzero. Define the
scattering angle $\theta\in[0,\pi]$ by
$$\theta:=\arccos\!\left(\frac{\mathbf p_1\cdot\mathbf k_1}{|\mathbf p_1|\,|\mathbf k_1|}\right),$$
using the Euclidean inner product on $\mathbb R^3$.
Write $g=\sqrt{4\pi\alpha}>0$, as in

$$ \beta_e=\sqrt{1-\frac{4m^2}{s}},\qquad \beta_\mu=\sqrt{1-\frac{4M^2}{s}}. $$

weight $1/4$ for the four initial spin-label pairs and sum over final spin
labels. Take the selected muon model charge to be $-e$ as well. Up to an
irrelevant common phase, its amplitude is
$$ \mathcal M_{\rm tree}=\frac{g^2}{s} [\bar v(p_2)\gamma^a u(p_1)] [\bar u(k_1)\gamma_a v(k_2)], $$
where the brackets denote the product of the two currents. This selected
formal amplitude adopts the current draft QFT-G02 line/vertex convention;
it is not an exact amplitude of a constructed continuum theory.

$\lambda^2(\hbar c)^2/(32\pi s)$ and the distinguishable result is twice

For fixed energy cutoffs $0<\lambda<\Lambda<\infty$ in joules, define
$\mathfrak h_E=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf q/[(2\pi)^3 2\omega];\mathbb C^2)$,
where $\omega=|\mathbf q|$, and
$$h_{\lambda,\Lambda,r}(\mathbf q) =g_{\mathrm{em}}J(q)\cdot\epsilon_r(\mathbf q/|\mathbf q|) \,\mathbf1_{\{\lambda<|\mathbf q|<\Lambda\}}.$$
The current draft mathematical supplier
[[thm-qft-example-soft-current-angular-coherent]] supplies the $\mathbb C^3$
transverse energy-space norm and unitary conversion. The measurable
orthonormal polarization frame gives the pointwise unitary identification
$h\mapsto\sum_{r=1}^2h_r\epsilon_r$ proved in step 3.1; composing it with
that conversion identifies $\mathfrak h_E$ with the positive transverse
one-particle space $\mathfrak h_T$ of [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]]
by the unitary map below, where for $\mathbf k\ne0$ the notation
$\epsilon_r(\mathbf k)$ denotes the homogeneous extension
$\epsilon_r(\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|)$ of the supplied sphere frame:
$$(U_Eh)(\mathbf k)= \sqrt{\frac{(\hbar c)^2}{(2\pi)^3\,2|\mathbf k|}} \sum_{r=1}^{2}h_r(\hbar c\,\mathbf k)\epsilon_r(\mathbf k), \qquad \mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}.$$
Here $\mathbf k$ is a wave vector in $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and
$\hbar c\,\mathbf k$ is the corresponding energy-momentum vector in joules.
Set $N_\gamma:=C\log(\Lambda/\lambda)$ and prepare the normalized coherent
vector in the free photon Fock space
$$\Psi_{\lambda,\Lambda} =e^{-N_\gamma/2}\bigoplus_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{(U_Eh_{\lambda,\Lambda})^{\otimes_s n}}{\sqrt{n!}} \in\mathcal F_s(\mathfrak h_T),$$
where the $n=0$ term is the vacuum sector. Let $P_n$ be the number-sector
projection from [[def-qft-x03-photon-count-pvm]] and define
$p_n$ as the model probability assigned to outcome $n$ by the finite
two-outcome projective partition $\{\{n\},\mathbb R\setminus\{n\}\}$.
Then
$$p_n=e^{-N_\gamma}\frac{N_\gamma^n}{n!},\qquad n\in\mathbb N_0,$$
with $0^0:=1$; these probabilities sum to one, the mean photon count is
$N_\gamma$, and the vacuum probability is $e^{-N_\gamma}$. The expected
photon energy is
$$\langle\Psi_{\lambda,\Lambda},H_\gamma\Psi_{\lambda,\Lambda}\rangle =C(\Lambda-\lambda)\ \mathrm J,$$
for $H_\gamma=\hbar c\,d\Gamma(|\mathbf k|)$ of
[[post-qft-free-photon-model]]. If $C>0$, the family has no Fock-norm or
projective-ray limit as $\lambda\downarrow0$ (projective-ray convergence means
norm convergence after allowing a unit-modulus phase for each cutoff), although
its mean energy tends to the finite value $C\Lambda$.

formal ring of [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]]. Let $\zeta$ denote finite graph
link data, $z$ a formal indeterminate, and
$K(z;\zeta)=K_0(\zeta)+zV(\zeta)\in M_d(\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket)$
with $d\ge1$ and $K_0(\zeta)\in GL_d(\mathbb C)$. For each vertex-angle
tuple $\theta$, let $\zeta^\theta$ and the invertible diagonal matrix
$D_\theta$ be the finite gauge action and phase matrix of
[[def-qft-qed-finite-graph-gauge-data]]. Assume the coefficient matrices
satisfy
$$K_0(\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta K_0(\zeta)D_\theta^{-1},\qquad V(\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta V(\zeta)D_\theta^{-1}.$$
Let $S(z;\zeta)$ be the coefficientwise formal inverse specified by
[[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]]. Then
$$S(z;\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta S(z;\zeta)D_\theta^{-1},\qquad \det K(z;\zeta^\theta)=\det K(z;\zeta).$$
For a real vertex tuple $\theta$, put
$\Theta=\operatorname{diag}_{x\in X}(\theta_xI_r)$,
$\zeta^s:=\zeta^{s\theta}$, and $D_s:=D_{s\theta}=e^{is\Theta}$.
For any coefficient family $A_s=A(z;\zeta^s)$, write
$\delta A:=\left.\frac{d}{ds}A_s\right|_{s=0}$ coefficientwise.
Assume also that
$K_0(\zeta^s)$ and $V(\zeta^s)$ vary differentiably along the gauge orbit
$\zeta^s$. Coefficientwise differentiation then gives
$$\delta S=i[\Theta,S]=-S(\delta K)S.$$
These are finite/formal identities only; the formal variable is not assigned
a numerical value and no convergence is asserted.

[F2] [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]]: $\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket$ uses
